//: Fleet-owned host allowlist, schema v2. ONE canonical list, two scopes:
'runtime' (a host a local agent run may reach at runtime) and 'fetch' (a
host an agent's own curl/wget/fetch may target directly — enforced by
fetch-allowlist-is-respected-at-edit + fetch-allowlist-is-respected-at-commit.mts). A
fetch-only host is a deliberate category - see the note further down.
PHASE 1 is plumbing only: mode is 'off' — nothing enforces egress yet.
INVARIANT: every runtime-scoped host must be a SUBSET of gh-aw's expanded
firewall allowDomains (the CI agent already trusts these) — enforced by
the fleet check-all gate. Grow this list only from traffic proven in the
observe soak, and only with a host gh-aw already permits. A leading '*.'
entry is a suffix wildcard (matches any subdomain of the suffix).
'allowDomains' is the pre-v2 key, DERIVED from the runtime-scoped hosts
(regenerate with check/fetch-allowlist-derived-copies-are-current.mts
--fix; never hand-edit it), kept so a member still on
an old bundled hook (which only reads allowDomains) sees no behavior
change during rollout. Drop it one soak window after every roster member
repins past the v2 reader.
'fetch'-without-'runtime' is a deliberate second category: a host with
real, evidenced fetch usage (a committed non-agentic file — a Dockerfile
RUN, a GH Actions step — OR a local-agent-only script/convenience that
never runs inside a gh-aw-fenced CI agent session) that has not been
PROVEN to need egress containment. Nothing enforces egress yet (mode is
'off'), so leaving these fetch-only changes zero real behavior versus the
pre-v2 ALLOWED_CDN_HOSTS list — it just defers the egress⊆gh-aw question
until someone actually needs one of these reachable from inside a gh-aw
session. dl.google.com / go.dev / static.rust-lang.org are proven by
fetch-allowlist-is-respected-at-commit.mts's own commit-time scan (a Dockerfile /
workflow literal). The rest — astral.sh, crates.io, badge.socket.dev,
api.fireworks.ai, api.openai.com, api.synthetic.new, claude.ai,
nodejs.org, sh.rustup.rs, socketusercontent.com — are the pre-v2 list's
own documented local-agent usages (spend meters, offload pickers, MCP
package-file reads, registry-infra state reads); none showed up in a
gh-aw lock measured 2026-08-20 in odai, the runner the fleet uses
(.github/workflows/weekly-update.lock.yml + get-green.lock.yml, 55 hosts
unioned). The wheelhouse itself carries no lock - it retired gh-aw for
keyless on-device workflows - so the subset gate is vacuous HERE and does
its containment work in the members that run agentic workflows.
because none of them are gh-aw-agent traffic in the first place.
Promoting any of these to 'runtime' needs BOTH real evidence the fetch
must survive inside a gh-aw session AND an explicit 'network.allowed'
addition in that session's gh-aw workflow source, recompiled and
re-measured here — not a default, and not required for fetch scope alone.

hosts.reason: gh release-asset redirects at runtime.
Anthropic API domain apex, alongside api.anthropic.com.

Anthropic's API — the Claude seat the spend meter measures, and one of the endpoints the model-availability poller probes (verify-state-before-acting for the tier env vars: a down alias fails the auto-mode permission classifier closed, so the probe is the read before the swap).

Fireworks' inference API — the default spend seat. fireworks-usage reads the month's spend from it, the offload model picker lists what it serves, and the availability poller probes its aliases before falling a tier back. Local-agent-only; fetch-only, see the file header.
GitHub's REST API — the external-tools updater reads a repo's release list to find the newest soak-cleared version, and the pinned-label gate resolves a tag to its sha.
The seat behind the codex offload route. Local-agent-only; fetch-only, see the file header.
Synthetic's API — synthetic-quota reads the request-rate window the gauge fills against, and the offload model picker lists what it serves. Local-agent-only; fetch-only, see the file header.
uv installer: curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh, fleet Python tooling. Local-agent-only; fetch-only, see the file header.

GitHub's avatar CDN — brand work reads a reference org/user avatar when a member logo derives from an upstream mark. Exact host, never a *.githubusercontent.com fetch target: raw./gist. content stay fetch-denied even though the egress wildcard above covers the redirect case.
Socket's own badge service — the fleet README skeleton's Socket Badge; agents verify badge markup/dimensions against the live SVG. Local-agent-only; fetch-only, see the file header.
Claude's subscription console — a usage read checks the seat's real level against the page the meter estimates. Local-agent-only; fetch-only, see the file header.

Claude Code documentation. Read-only reference for the hook events, settings keys and tool names the fleet hook tree is written against; consulted when an artifact shape needs grounding in the upstream contract rather than in this repo’s own copy of it.
gh CLI / git archive download redirects.

The Rust package registry's public API — the cargo registry-infra (registry.mts, trusted-publisher.mts, crate-release-sha.mts) reads crate state before acting (verify-state-before-acting). Local-agent-only; fetch-only, see the file header.
Google Chrome stable .deb — .github/workflows/on-device-model-cache.yml's odai chrome-builtin provisioning step. Non-agentic CI step; fetch-only, see the file header.
GitHub Container Registry image pulls.
GitHub release-asset CDN redirect target.
gh CLI (release assets, clones, API) + release-asset downloads; fleet-wide.
Go toolchain download — docker/fleet/go-base.Dockerfile. Non-agentic Docker build step; fetch-only, see the file header.
Git LFS object transfer.
Official Node.js distribution host for versioned source and binary archives. Local-agent-only; fetch-only, see the file header.
GitHub release-asset CDN redirect target.
